column1: # comment: "AI / RAG / GraphRAG claim-layer alignments (#54). PROV-O: the activity spine (ModelInvocation/RetrievalEvent/EvaluationRun are prov:Activity by inheritance \u2014 the parent gmeow:Activity cell carries that; here only the AI-specific seams are added). ML-Schema: mls:Run is the W3C member-submission counterpart of a model invocation; mls:Model the trained-model artifact. schema.org: schema:Claim is the published claim documented in fact-checking markup \u2014 GMEOW's Claim is broader (any contestable assertion with statement-level epistemics), so closeMatch; the principled REFUSAL of schema:ClaimReview's single reviewRating verdict is recorded in the trailer. Web Annotation: an EvidenceSpan grounding a claim is near-isomorphic to an oa:Annotation whose target is the chunk with selectors; the full projection is #55's deliverable. Wikidata: hub identifiers for the headline concepts."

# # REFUSED (Principle 5/9 — verdict semantics): schema:ClaimReview. Its single reviewRating adjudicates a winner; GMEOW contradictions coexist standpoint-indexed, surfaced by gmeow:Contradiction and never resolved by rank.
# # REFUSED (Principle 5 — no faithful term): gmeow:Embedding / gmeow:VectorIndex have no external RDF counterpart (the #54 survey's genuine gap); cells will be added when a standard emerges.
# # REFUSED (Principle 5 — scope mismatch): C2PA assertions sign MEDIA provenance at the container level, not statement-level claims; the attestation slice owns that seam.

column6: schema:Claim is the fact-check-markup claim; GMEOW's carries statement-level confidence/standpoint/time the schema.org term lacks
Wikidata 'word embedding' family — the vector-representation concept; no RDF vocabulary exists (the #54 gap)
mls:Model is the trained artifact itself; the ModelCard is the description of one — the nearest stable RDF term (Model Cards have no canonical RDF vocabulary)
ML-Schema's Run is the executed model task; GMEOW's invocation adds prompt + sampling provenance
a prompt is a prov:Entity used by the invocation activity; PROV-O has nothing finer
in the Web Annotation projection (#55) the claim is the annotation body and the evidence span its target; the property directions differ, hence relatedMatch
